Ipamorelin in the US: The Selective Secretagogue

A pentapeptide whose defining property is what it does not do, and a certificate check that suits a small molecule

June 18, 2026·By Adam Reeves · Research Editor, Eppix Labs

Ipamorelin is defined in the literature by a negative result, which is unusual and worth taking seriously. Raun et al. (1998) characterized it as the first selective growth hormone secretagogue: it released GH in their models without the prolactin and ACTH elevation that accompanied earlier compounds in the class.[1] Selectivity, not potency, is the property the paper is about.

This guide covers the molecule, the published work, and the certificate checks. Ipamorelin is supplied for laboratory research use only.

What ipamorelin is

Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor GHS-R1a, the same receptor ghrelin acts on. Two of its five residues are non-natural (α-aminoisobutyric acid at position 1, D-2-naphthylalanine at position 3), one more is a D-amino acid, and the C-terminus is amidated. Those modifications are what give a five-residue peptide enough metabolic stability to be useful.

Mechanistically it sits on the opposite side of the GH axis from the GHRH analogs: CJC-1295, sermorelin and tesamorelin act at the GHRH receptor, ipamorelin at the ghrelin receptor. That is why the two classes are studied together, and why they are sold together.

Sequence and structure

Five residues, around 712 Da, with three non-standard positions. The non-natural residues are the quality-relevant detail: a supplier substituting L-phenylalanine for D-phenylalanine, or plain alanine for Aib, produces a peptide with a different mass and different behaviour that a purity assay would happily report as pure. Identity by mass spectrometry is the check that catches it.

What the published research shows

A small, coherent literature centred on the original development program:

  • ·Characterization and selectivity. Raun et al. (1998): GH release in rat and swine models with the selectivity profile that gave the compound its name in the literature.[1]
  • ·Longitudinal bone growth. Johansen et al. (1999) reported increased longitudinal bone growth in rats on repeated administration.[2]
  • ·Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss. Andersen et al. (2001) reported that ipamorelin counteracted glucocorticoid-induced decrease in bone formation in adult rats.[3]

The limit of the evidence

Ipamorelin entered early clinical investigation and was not carried through development. There are no published randomized efficacy trials, no approved indication in any jurisdiction, no established human dose, and no human safety record of meaningful size. the FDA has authorized nothing containing it.

The selectivity result is a preclinical finding in specific animal models. It is frequently repeated as though it were a human clinical characterization, which it is not.

Verifying an ipamorelin lot

Identity by mass spectrometry against the expected mass near 712 Da, HPLC purity, and measured content against the labeled amount. For a peptide this small, measured content is the figure that most directly affects what you paid for: a 10 mg label with 6 mg in the vial is a 40% loss that purity data cannot reveal.

Every Eppix ipamorelin lot is tested by Janoshik Analytical, published before sale and verifiable on the laboratory's own database.

Frequently Asked

What makes ipamorelin "selective"?

In the 1998 characterization, it released GH in animal models without the prolactin and ACTH elevation that accompanied earlier growth hormone secretagogues. Selectivity in this sense refers to that preclinical finding, not to a human clinical characterization.

Is ipamorelin legal in the US?

It may be sold and held as a laboratory research material. It is not approved by the FDA for human or veterinary use. This is not legal advice.

How does ipamorelin differ from CJC-1295?

Different receptors. Ipamorelin agonizes the ghrelin receptor GHS-R1a; CJC-1295 is a GHRH-receptor analog. They are studied and sold together because they engage the same axis from two directions.

What should an ipamorelin certificate show?

Batch number matching the vial, the named testing laboratory with an independent verification path, MS identity against the expected mass near 712 Da, HPLC purity, and measured content against the labeled amount.

Are there human trials of ipamorelin?

It entered early clinical investigation and was not developed further. There are no published randomized efficacy trials and no approved indication anywhere.

How is ipamorelin stored?

Lyophilized: cool, dry, dark, at -20 °C for long-term storage. Reconstituted: refrigerated, used within the window your protocol defines.
